item.title: When the sun rises, bhikkhus, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely the dawn. So too, bhikkhus, for wholesome states, this is the…
item.description:
When the sun rises, bhikkhus, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely the dawn. So too, bhikkhus, for wholesome states, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely right view. From right view, bhikkhus, comes right intention. From right intention comes right speech. From right speech comes right action. From right action comes right livelihood. From right livelihood comes right effort. From right effort comes right mindfulness. From right mindfulness comes right concentration. From right concentration comes right knowledge. From right knowledge comes right liberation.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.121

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of purity. What three? Purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of purity. What three? Purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of purity.

Purity of body and speech,
Purity of mind, without taints,
One who is pure, possessing purity,
Is called one who has abandoned all.

From: Itivuttaka 66

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a fisherman casts a baited hook into a deep lake. A fish, looking at the bait, swallows the hook. Thus, bhikkhus, that…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a fisherman casts a baited hook into a deep lake. A fish, looking at the bait, swallows the hook. Thus, bhikkhus, that fish, having swallowed the fisherman's hook, falls into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the fisherman's mercy. So too, bhikkhus, there are these six hooks in the world, bringing misfortune to beings, bringing calamity to creatures. What six? Bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in those forms, praises them, and abides with attachment, then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who has swallowed Māra's hook, who has fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the Evil One's mercy. ... There are sounds cognizable by the ear ... odors cognizable by the nose ... tastes cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body ... There are mind-objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in those mind-objects, praises them, and abides with attachment, then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who has swallowed Māra's hook, who has fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the Evil One's mercy.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.230

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu goes to a forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, and reflects thus: 'It is…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu goes to a forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, and reflects thus: 'It is not for the sake of robes that I have gone forth from home to homelessness. It is not for the sake of almsfood, not for the sake of lodging, not for the sake of this or that state of existence that I have gone forth from home to homelessness. But rather, thinking: "I am subject to birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; I am subject to suffering, overwhelmed by suffering. Perhaps the complete destruction of this whole mass of suffering can be made known." And having gone forth from home to homelessness, if I were to pursue sensual desires again, even worse than before, that would not be proper for me.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.40

item.title: Happy indeed we live, Without hatred among the hateful. Among hateful people, We dwell without hatred. Happy indeed we live, Without illness among the ill.…
item.description:
Happy indeed we live,
Without hatred among the hateful.
Among hateful people,
We dwell without hatred.

Happy indeed we live,
Without illness among the ill.
Among ill people,
We dwell without illness.

Happy indeed we live,
Without restlessness among the restless.
Among restless people,
We dwell without restlessness.

Happy indeed we live,
We who have nothing called our own.
We shall feed on joy,
Like the radiant devas.

From: Dhammapada 197-208

item.title: Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live practicing deceit, speaking flattery, hinting, belittling, and seeking gain by means…
item.description:
Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live practicing deceit, speaking flattery, hinting, belittling, and seeking gain by means of gain — Samaṇa Gotama abstains from such deceit and flattery. — Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 1 – Brahmajālasutta

item.title: Ānanda, if any bhikkhu, bhikkhunī, male lay follower, or female lay follower lives in accordance with the Dhamma, rightly in the Dhamma, practicing the Dhamma…
item.description:
Ānanda, if any bhikkhu, bhikkhunī, male lay follower, or female lay follower lives in accordance with the Dhamma, rightly in the Dhamma, practicing the Dhamma properly, that person honors, respects, reveres, and makes offerings to the Tathāgata with the supreme offering. Therefore, Ānanda, you should live in accordance with the Dhamma, rightly in the Dhamma, and practice the Dhamma properly. Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise: 'As the moon in the sky, With clouds…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise:

'As the moon in the sky,
With clouds cleared away,
Shining like the sun,
Pure, without defilement.
So you, the Great Muni,
The noble sage,
Your fame shines brightly,
Surpassing all worlds.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 8.11

item.title: Enduring cold and heat, Hunger and thirst, Wind and sun, flies and snakes, Live alone like a rhinoceros. Like a great elephant with massive shoulders,…
item.description:
Enduring cold and heat,
Hunger and thirst,
Wind and sun, flies and snakes,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

Like a great elephant with massive shoulders,
Leaving the herd, living in the forest as it pleases,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.3

item.title: A bhikkhu who controls his mouth, Speaks moderately, without conceit, When explaining the Dhamma's meaning, His words are gentle and sweet. A bhikkhu who delights…
item.description:
A bhikkhu who controls his mouth,
Speaks moderately, without conceit,
When explaining the Dhamma's meaning,
His words are gentle and sweet.

A bhikkhu who delights in the Dhamma,
Who loves the Dhamma and reflects on the Dhamma,
Who remembers the true Dhamma,
Does not fall away from the true Dhamma.

One should not despise what one receives,
Nor envy the gains of others.
A bhikkhu who envies others
Does not attain concentration.

Though a bhikkhu receives little,
He should not despise his own gain.
Living pure, not lazy,
Even devas praise such a one.

From: Dhammapada 360-382
